transcript.answer:
Short answer
- Root cause: The ledger-api processes on rcabench-worker2 hit "Too many open files" (Errno 24) shortly after the 1.4.2 rollout. That made the app stop accepting connections (503 on probe), so the kubelet marked those pods NotReady. The failure is localized to the three pods on node rcabench-worker2.

What I confirmed
- Affected pods (Ready = false) — all running APP_VERSION=1.4.2 on image python:3.12-alpine:
  - ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 (node rcabench-worker2, IP 10.244.1.15)
  - ledger-api-866db84748-cz4wp (node rcabench-worker2, IP 10.244.1.13)
  - ledger-api-866db84748-vv6jk (node rcabench-worker2, IP 10.244.1.14)
- Healthy pods (Ready = true) are on rcabench-worker (three pods).
- Pod events show readiness probe failures starting at ~2026-10-07T09:44Z with connection refused, later HTTP 503.
- Application logs on the failing pods show repeated errors starting ~2026-10-07T09:45:3Z:
  - "ERROR ledger-api accept failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files"
  - These errors repeat every ~10s up to the end of the log sample.
- Node rcabench-worker2 is Ready and shows no Memory/Disk/PID pressure in the node description; the problem is not general node crash but per-process file descriptor exhaustion.

Why that points to the root cause
- Errno 24 ("Too many open files") is the canonical kernel error when a process reaches its RLIMIT_NOFILE or the kernel/global file limit; when the process can't accept new sockets, HTTP handlers return 5xx/connection refused and readiness probes fail.
- The issue only affected pods scheduled on rcabench-worker2, so it’s either:
  1) A per-node/container runtime limit (lower ulimits or container runtime default_ulimits on rcabench-worker2), or
  2) A file-descriptor leak / much higher concurrentfd usage in the ledger-api 1.4.2 build that pushed processes over the limit — the leak would surface first on the subset of pods with the worst load or lowest FD limits.
- The sequence matches: startup → some work → Errno 24 → readiness probe 503 → kubelet marks pod NotReady.

Immediate mitigations (fast, safe)
1. Restart/reschedule the affected pods (temporary fix) — can clear the FD state:
   - kubectl rollout restart deployment ledger-api -n ledger
     or
   - kubectl delete pod <pod> -n ledger for each affected pod (kube will recreate them).
   Note: restarting may only be temporary if the root cause is a leak or limit that will be hit again.

2. Evacuate the node (if you want pods moved away from rcabench-worker2):
   - kubectl cordon rcabench-worker2
   - kubectl drain rcabench-worker2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
   This forces pods to reschedule on other nodes where they previously were OK.

3. If you need immediate rollback:
   - kubectl -n ledger set image deployment/ledger-api api=<previous-image-or-tag>
   - Or rollback the release if you use helm.

Commands to run now to confirm details (run on your cluster)
- Check per-process limits inside an affected pod:
  - kubectl exec -n ledger -it ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 -- sh -c 'cat /proc/1/limits | grep -i nofile'
  - kubectl exec -n ledger -it ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4 -- sh -c 'ls /proc/1/fd | wc -l'
- Check global/node file descriptor limit:
  - kubectl get node rcabench-worker2 -o name
  - ssh to node or run a privileged pod to check:
    - sysctl fs.file-max
    - ulimit -n (for the kubelet/ processes; requires node access)
- Check container runtime default ulimits (Docker) or containerd config (containerd) on rcabench-worker2:
  - For Docker: cat /etc/docker/daemon.json | jq .default-ulimits
  - For containerd: check /etc/containerd/config.toml for rlimit settings

Medium-term fixes (pick what fits)
1. Fix the app if it leaks FDs or keeps sockets open:
   - Audit connection handling, database clients, file handles; add proper close/finalize.
   - Limit concurrency or use connection pooling.

2. Raise file descriptor limits for containers on the problematic nodes:
   - If using Docker, set default-ulimits in daemon.json and restart docker.
   - For containerd, set rlimits in its config or start containers with the required limits (depends on runtime).
   - Increase node fs.file-max if you see global exhaustion (sysctl fs.file-max=...).

3. Make the pod robust:
   - Add a liveness probe that restarts the process if it becomes unresponsive.
   - Add resource requests/limits (CPU/memory) and a reasonable readiness probe timeout to avoid flapping.
   - Add startupProbe if service needs more time to warm up.

4. Instrument and alert:
   - Export process FD usage metrics (e.g., process_open_fds in node exporter or an app metric) and create alert on high fd count.
   - Alert when readiness probe fails with HTTP 5xx repeatedly.

Suggested next steps I can run for you
- Confirm the exact per-process RLIMIT_NOFILE and current /proc/<pid>/fd count by exec'ing into one failing pod.
- Check the other node's configuration (rcabench-worker) for ulimits or runtime diffs to see why it's unaffected.
- If you want, I can run the kubectl exec/log/describe commands now (need your go-ahead) and collect the exact limit numbers and fd counts and prepare a short remediation playbook.

Summary (one line)
- ledger-api pods on rcabench-worker2 hit "Too many open files" (Errno 24) after the 1.4.2 rollout, causing the app to stop accepting connections and the kubelet to mark them NotReady. Fix by either fixing the FD leak in the app or raising container/node file-descriptor limits; restart or reschedule pods as a short-term recovery.
